author: Robert Mackey
description:
Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’

Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.

Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Se
title: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Verdict in case against former Uber driver Jonathan Rinderknecht comes after first trial ended with hung jury

The 30-year-old accused of sparking the deadly Palisades fire in Los Angeles was found guilty of two federal arson charges in a Friday verdict that came months after his first trial concluded with a hung jury.

For two weeks, a fresh batch of jurors listened to prosecutors mount their case against Jonathan Rinderknecht.

Continue reading...
title: Man accused of sparking deadly Los Angeles wildfire found guilty

author: Marina Dunbar
description:
Although there is no definitive link between violent video games and behavior, departments take to social media

While critics have been raving after the recent and long-awaited arrival of Grand Theft Auto VI, the latest entry in the famously violent video game series has also prompted real-world warnings from authorities.

Police departments across the US met the game’s release on Thursday with reminders that the car thefts, reckless driving, violence and other criminal mayhem depicted in the blockbuster title should not be re-enacted on the country’s streets.

Continue reading...
title: US police departments warn GTA VI users to ‘keep it in the game’

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Comedian Stavros Halkias voices fictional shock jock

  • Segment echoes Watson, Tucker misconduct allegations

  • Rockstar’s latest skewers American sports culture

The long-awaited Grand Theft Auto VI appears to have taken aim at the NFL’s sexual misconduct scandals – and the culture of excuses surrounding them – with a satirical segment on the video game’s fictional conservative talk radio station bearing striking similarities to allegations against Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson and Kansas City Chiefs kicker Justin Tucker.

The segment features comedian and voice actor Stavros Halkias defending Anthony Ross, a fictional player for the Vice City Manatees, after an “alleged” incident involving a team masseuse. Although neither Watson nor Tucker are mentioned by name, the circumstances closely resemble allegations made against both players.
title: Grand Theft Auto VI appears to mock NFL sexual misconduct scandals in radio parody

author: Ben Doherty
description:
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi

Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

Continue reading...
title: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ on US tech firms that build datacenters abroad

author: Dani Anguiano
description:
Scientists reared the San Francisco natives through their vulnerable youth before setting them free in nature

San Francisco garter snakes born and raised in a zoo-based conservation program have been released into the wild for the first time as part of an effort to save what is considered one of North America’s most beautiful snakes.

The non-venomous reptiles are known for their striking colors – red heads, turquoise bellies and vibrant red and black stripes on their sides. The species, found only on the San Francisco peninsula, has been listed as endangered for more than half a century.

Continue reading...
title: Striking snakes released into the wild in historic fight to save species from extinction

author: Pablo Iglesias Maurer
description:
Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one

In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’ve done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday.

In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinit
title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it

author: Guardian sport and agencies
description:
• Get-in price peaked at $755 before dropping to $362

  • Previous NWSL finals never topped $100 on matchday

  • Analyst cites Spirit home game and thin resale supply

The get-in price for tickets to Saturday’s NWSL Championship match plunged more than 50% this week but was still set to finish at more than three times the previous record for an NWSL final.

After the Washington Spirit booked their spot in the final against the Kansas City Current with a semi-final victory last Saturday, the get-in price for the championship match spiked as high as $755 that same night, according to TicketData.com. However, that price had dropped as low as $308 on Friday morning before climbing back to
title: NWSL final tickets top $350 in ‘perfect storm’ even after fall from $755 peak

author: David Hytner
description:
Argentinian has excelled in man-management – but will need his powers to energise new squad and impress owners

Mauricio Pochettino celebrated his 50th birthday in style. It was March 2022, he was in charge at Paris Saint-Germain and the venue was a stunning boutique hotel; the kind that many capitals have but only Paris truly does. Pochettino’s family and friends were there. So were his inner coaching circle, who are basically family. There were lots of people from PSG. And a good time was had by all.

For Pochettino, it was emotional. As everybody knows, the new Manchester United head coach is the kind of guy to well up when the speeches start, so imagine how he felt when he looked up at the big screen and a video montage of well-wishers started to roll.
title: Pochettino the connector: will human touch lift Manchester United?

author: Giles Richards in Las Vegas
description:
George Russell calls it the biggest race on the Formula One calendar bar Monaco – and the numbers back him up

That Formula One has achieved a palpable success in hosting a race in Las Vegas is impossible to ignore. Even with this year’s outing a dead rubber and with the city in perhaps its least flattering light, the cold drizzle of a Thursday afternoon beneath gunmetal-grey skies, the fans who have flocked to Nevada were irrepressibly enthusiastic.

Long queues stretched out into the streets before the gates were even open and it seems even many locals who were initially cool to the somewhat disruptive F1 circus have embraced the fans, their fervour for the sport and the positive impact of the race.

Continue reading...
title: The Super Bowl of F1: how Las Vegas GP has hit the jackpot after turbulent start

author: Sam Cunningham
description:
The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player

Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality.

He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session.

Continue reading...
title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet

author: Barney Ronay
description:
The encroachment of artificial intelligence smells like the death of sport. Can we find the will and collective backbone to resist?

There was an interesting development this week in the endless rolling mega-froth over tech billionaire Jensen Huang, a saga that may or may not have involved some kind of adulterous 63-year-old honey trap spy dynamic.

The latest suggestion being punted about is that, whatever his raw human frailties, Huang is in fact “irreplaceable” as the president of Nvidia. Only this guy can do it. Only this leather-jacketed human visionary, who looks in every available photo like your GCSE chemistry teacher’s profile pic on TerrifiedUkrainianSinglesWantToDateYou.com, can manage this key artificial intelligence mission.
title: Forget rogue robots, it’s tech billionaires and AI cricket that should really terrify us | Barney Ronay

author: Graham Readfearn, Fiona Harvey and Damien Gayle in Antalya, Turkey
description:
African ministers say they ‘didn’t come here to beg’, with civil society groups calling it the ‘worst Cop ever’

Crucial climate talks headed into overtime on the last official day of the Cop31 UN summit as countries continued to argue over a draft deal that was silent on fossil fuels, with a host of other contentious issues complicating negotiations.

Nearly 200 countries struggled to bridge their differences after two weeks of intense talks and impassioned speeches in Antalya, Turkey, about the effects of climate breakdown around the world, with a scheduled finish of Friday evening breached.

Continue reading...
title: Cop31 talks go into overtime as fossil fuels vanish from draft deal

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with John Collingridge ; produced by Angus Neale ; senior producer Leonore Schick ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
The AI firm and Claude chatbot maker Anthropic has made a historic stock market debut, with a peak valuation of $1.3tn on its first day of trading. It marks a remarkable ascent for a start-up launched in just 2021 by a group of ex-OpenAI staffers. Anthropic’s CEO, Dario Amodei, said the record-breaking IPO had ‘strengthened’ the company’s resolve to ‘do the right thing’. Despite the excitement, the Guardian’s head of business John Collingridge tells Lucy Hough that there are still challenges ahead for the global AI industry

Continue reading...
title: Is Claude creator Anthropic really worth $1.5 trillion? - The Latest

author: Timothy Pratt
description:
Pro-Palestinian donor James ‘Fergie’ Chambers released as court considers extradition request

In a blur of events surrounding the Trump administration’s effort to extradite James “Fergie” Chambers, Spain released the wealthy US activist and donor on bail even as Irish police raided a Dublin house owned by Chambers and his partner, Stella Schnabel, acting on a request from US authorities.

Chambers’s case is the first known instance of the US seeking to extradite a citizen over alleged support for Hamas, an accusation apparently tied to an international money-laundering charge in the criminal complaint underpinning the extradition request and donations to organizations helping Palestinians in Gaza.

Continue reading...
title: Spain frees wealthy US-sought activist on bail as Irish police raid Dublin home

author: Greg Wood
description:
Abuse and threats are becoming a grimly familiar part of daily routine for riders, confirms jockeys’ association

When Nico de Boinville received a security escort back to his car after racing at Plumpton on Monday, following a telephone threat to harm the jockey received at Nicky Henderson’s stable, it was the first time that such a move had received widespread media attention.

It was not, however, the first time that it had been felt necessary to give a rider additional protection at a racecourse. James Bowen said on Friday, in a blog for the bookmaker Dragonsports, that he and his brother, Sean, the champion over jumps, “were both the subject of death threats” during a meeting at Ffos Las in October 2025, “to the extent that we had security accompanying us between the paddock and weighing room for the next three or four days.”
title: Racing rocked by death threats to Bowens after De Boinville security incident

author: Martin Rowson
description: Continue reading...
title: Martin Rowson on the summits in Shenzhen and Brussels – cartoon

author: Sian Cain
description:
From Colin from Accounts to a certain blue heeler dog, Australian TV has swept the globe – so much so that many kids have picked up the accent. Homegrown stars and creators explain how down under went overground

About four years ago, parents around the world began observing a strange phenomena in their children: Australian accents. Bluey – the charming cartoon about a dog and her family that is currently one of the most watched shows in the world – had children saying words such as “dunny” and “brekky” without thinking twice.

“When I was a kid, I would do an American accent when I played with my toys,” says Daley Pearson, co-founder of Ludo Studio, which makes Bluey. “So this is like the colony taking back over!”

Continue reading...
title: ‘It’s peak Aussie – and it’s fantastic!’ How Australian TV conquered the world

author: Adrienne Matei
description:
Experts say there are many reasons to boost our consumption of mushrooms and incorporate them into our diets

Mushrooms aren’t quite as popular in the US as they are in other parts of the world. On average, Americans eat just shy of 4lb (1.81kg) of mushrooms per capita each year, while in South Korea people eat almost 6lb (2.72kg) a year, and in Japan, that number is closer to 12lb (5.44kg).

People in the US also don’t consume as wide a variety of mushrooms as other parts of the world, says Dr Krystle Zuniga, a board-certified oncology dietitian based in Austin, Texas. “I often think of them as a forgotten vegetable,” she says, though she clarifies they are technically fungi.

Con
title: Vitamin D, fiber and flavor: how healthy are mushrooms?

author: Sachin Nakrani in New York
description:
• New York City major hurt in friendly with press corps

  • Lifelong Gunner set to be out of action for nine months

Arsenal have suffered a further injury blow after it was revealed that one of their most famous supporters, New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, tore his achilles while playing in a friendly soccer match on Thursday and is out of action until next summer.

Not long after Mikel Arteta confirmed Bukayo Saka may not return to action before Christmas as he continues rehabilitation from a thigh injury, Mamdani added to Gunners woe by outlining how and why he is also sidelined for some time during a press conference that began with him announcing plans to close the Rikers Island jail complex.
title: Fresh injury blow for Arsenal as Zohran Mamdani is sidelined with achilles tear

author: Guardian sport and Press Association
description:
Playmaker returns from suspension, while Enzo Maresca acknowledges his midfield needs balance

Continue reading...
title: Premier League news: Grealish available again for Everton, Maresca hints at City tweaks

author: Ben Child
description:
The actor’s new role as James Bond could be bad news for DC, as a new owner, new chief and new director already threaten to shake and stir Gotham’s distinctive hero

Can one actor play both Batman and James Bond? This is the question many have been asking since Robert Pattinson was announced as the new 007. The obvious answer is yes: the 40-year-old Englishman has the poise, charisma and steel to join His Majesty’s Secret Service, and saving Gotham could soon become something he fits in between assignments.

Among all the furore over Pattinson’s appointment, it would have been easy to miss some rather less cheering news for the citizens of Gotham. According to the Wrap, delays to The Batman: Part II have freed the actor from his contractual ob
title: Delays mean Robert Pattinson doesn’t have to do a third Batman movie. DC Studios had better persuade him – and fast

author: Associated Press
description:
Bipartisan legislation now goes to the House amid concerns by some Democrats and environmental groups

The Senate approved bipartisan legislation on Thursday aimed at speeding up permitting reviews to build power plants, transmission lines and other energy infrastructure as lawmakers seek to increase the nation’s energy supplies to meet surging demand and lower electricity prices.

The legislation’s sweeping changes would shorten the timeline to start big energy projects and make sure datacenters pay for the energy they use. Anger over datacenters and rising electricity prices helped usher in a wave of Democrats pledging to clamp down on the energy-hungry behemoths.

Continue reading...
title: US Senate approves bill to speed up permitting reviews for energy projects and datacenters

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Flowers and notes appeared next to sculpture of hippos at Cincinnati zoo within hours of Fiona dying, days after swallowing a visitor’s hat

Tributes are pouring in and an impromptu shrine has popped up at the Cincinnati zoo in Ohio as fans of the famous hippopotamus Fiona mourn the animal’s death on Thursday, following failed attempts to save her after she ate a knitted hat.

Flowers and notes began appearing next to a sculpture of hippos at the zoo within hours of Fiona dying on Thursday despite numerous treatments aiming to help her eliminate the object that got stuck in her digestive tract.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Forever our Fiona’: fans of the famous hippo mourn her death at zoo

author: Bryan Armen Graham
description:
When does it start? Who’s tipped to win? And why isn’t Magnus Carlsen playing? We (mostly) have the answers

  • Play through 22 famous world championship games

India’s Gukesh Dommaraju is making his first defense of the world chess championship against fast-rising Uzbek star Javokhir Sindarov over the next three weeks in the affluent Geneva suburb of Cologny. Both players are 20 years old, making it the youngest matchup in the 140-year history of the sport’s most coveted title.

But is that all you need to know? What about the format, how much they’re getting paid and why the world’s No 1-ranked player is watch
title: World Chess Championship 2026: Gukesh Dommaraju v Javokhir Sindarov match questions, answered

author: Exclusive by Matt Hughes
description:
• NFL legend was Chelsea guest at Club World Cup

  • Brady has good relationship with Behdad Eghbali

Tom Brady is in discussions about buying a small stake in Chelsea. The NFL legend sold a minority share in Birmingham City after three years this month, a move sources have told the Guardian was to pave the way for investing at Stamford Bridge.

Brady was a guest of Chelsea when Enzo Maresca’s then side won the Club World Cup in New Jersey last year and was seen celebrating with the players after their remarkable 3-0 final win over Paris Saint-Germain.

Continue reading...
title: Tom Brady in talks over buying Chelsea stake after Birmingham City exit

author: Joanna Partridge
description:
Three Choirs unveils its First Release white wine after warm summer led to its earliest harvest start in 50 years

Forget beaujolais nouveau: a Gloucestershire vineyard has uncorked its 2026 vintage, giving the first taste of this year’s long, hot summer – and an answer to France’s autumn tradition of opening young wine straight after harvest.

Three Choirs near Newent has unveiled its First Release white wine after the earliest harvest in its 50 years of producing wine.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Gloucestershire nouveau’: UK vineyard uncorks its 2026 answer to beaujolais

author: Penelope Green
description:
A daily ocean swimmer, documentary photographer Penelope Green captures scenes of sanguine oceangoers embracing the elements in Newcastle and beyond, with a focus on communities interacting with the natural landscape. Her first solo exhibition, Sea of Life, is on now until 26 November at The Garden Gallery in Sydney’s Royal Botanic Garden

Continue reading...
title: To be beside the sea: the joy of Australian beach rituals – in pictures

author: Munther Emad
description:
After two attempts at two separate border crossings, I was denied entry, despite an approved visa and an official invitation from my health diplomacy charity

This month I set out to return to Palestine, where I was born and studied, as part of a health diplomacy delegation to the occupied Palestinian territories and Israel. After two attempts at two separate border crossings, I was denied entry, despite an approved visa and an official invitation from the charity on whose board I sit, Rozana. The alleged reason is that I hold a Gaza ID, even though I haven’t lived there for 28 years.

Rozana trains Palestinian doctors and nurses in Israeli hospitals and transports patients from the West Bank and Gaza to critical care. My mission as a board director of Rozana Australia is to advocate for dialogue through healthcare collaboration. I have seen the power of this work up close, and I believe it can pave the way for Palestinians and Israelis to recognise their shared need for
title: I’m an Australian-Palestinian doctor who was turned away at the West Bank border. The stigma of being born in Gaza stands in the way of peace

author: Martin Pegan
description:
The wheel has turned in a way nobody could have scripted eight years ago with Australia’s former Test captain in the frame to take back the reins

Australian cricket is back talking itself into circles around “sandpapergate” more than eight years after a ball tampering agent was taken on to the field in Cape Town.

Usman Khawaja’s autobiography, David Warner’s continued commentary, Pat Cummins’ 68-minute press conference and Cameron Bancroft’s 4,000-word first-person account have added fuel to the fire that has engulfed Australian cricket all over again. But there is one voice we are yet to hear from, and his silence is speaking louder than words.

Continue reading...
title: Steve Smith’s silence speaks louder than words to reshape his sandpapergate legacy | Martin Pegan

author: Amy Batey-McManus
description:
The queer female characters in Netflix’s Catholic school girl horror series are messy and relatable – and unreasonably rare

I haven’t been able to get away from Netflix’s The Body. Since the show’s release this month, it’s taken over my conversations and social feeds, and seems to be consuming the collective consciousness of every lesbian I know. Every reel I come across has already been liked by someone in my extended web of gays. The algorithm seems to understand me and, judging by the numbers, plenty of other people too.

Set in 2004, the psychological horror-drama follows a female Catholic high school dance troupe whose botched Halloween initiation ritual triggers prophetic visions, town-wide mass hysteria and a repressed sapphic yearning between its leads, Anya (Kristina Bogic) and Elise (Sara Boustany).

Continue reading...
title: The Body is a hit – and every lesbian I know is obsessed. Why aren’t there more sapphic stories on screen?

author: Bryan Armen Graham
description:
As Gukesh Dommaraju and Javokhir Sindarov meet across the board in Geneva, revisit 22 classic games from the world chess championship’s 140-year history

The newest chapter in the 140-year history of the world chess championship will be written over the next three weeks in Geneva, where Gukesh Dommaraju of India will defend his title against Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov. The two 20-year-olds will make history as the youngest ever pairing to contest for the sport’s most coveted title, joining a roll call of great players whose encounters have helped define the game itself.

From the middle of the 16th century, the names of chess players who have been widely regarded as the strongest of their time have been passed down. The earliest of these was the Spanish priest Ruy López de Segura, after whom one of the most popular openings of modern times is named. Oth
title: From Bobby Fischer to Magnus Carlsen: 22 of the most famous world chess championship games

author: Rowena Mason Whitehall editor
description:
Farage issues warning to potential rivals and says he will fight next election as leader if ‘still here and fit and healthy’

Nigel Farage has said he does not see another person who could do his job as leader of Reform UK, in a warning shot to potential rivals who might seek to replace him.

The Reform UK leader delivered a message that he was going nowhere despite his worries over his personal safety in the wake of the killing of the Reform politician Ann Widdecombe.

Continue reading...
title: No one else in Reform is suitable to lead the party, Nigel Farage says

author: Owen Lewis
description:
After a humiliating NBA finals defeat, Victor Wembanyama has returned with a vengeance – and the Spurs look like contenders again

It wouldn’t be exactly right to say Victor Wembanyama didn’t miss a beat after a disastrous NBA finals in June that left him and his San Antonio Spurs defeated, memed and embarrassed. In the Spurs’ first game this season, against an Oklahoma City Thunder team since decimated by injuries, Wemby went an appalling 1-for-13 from the field. Ten of his 12 points came via free throws. After getting blocked by Aday Mara, the Thunder’s 7ft 3in offseason pickup clearly designed to counter the even more towering Wembanyama, he leaned over his knees and muttered furiously to himself as if trying to exorcise an intrusive thought. It brought to mind an image from the NBA finals a few months earlier: Wemby on the floor after being fouled by the Knicks’ Mitchell Robinson, crowing, “I’m in your head!” The Spurs
title: Victor Wembanyama has turned his NBA finals humiliation into a revenge tour for the ages

author: Dana R Fisher
description:
Political participation – in meetings, boycotts and demonstrations – has increased since Trump took office. It’s time for change

Over the past two years, Americans have watched as the Trump administration enacted Project 2025 and the US has descended into a state of lawless authoritarianism. Instead of sinking into a state of paralysis, though, Americans rose up to push back against the attacks, including limitations of voting rights and manipulations of political power through the gerrymandering of congressional districts.

Donald Trump’s actions motivated resistance in the streets in the form of large-scale public demonstrations, along with more localized mobilizations against ICE and the occupation of American cities. On 3 November, the collective response manifested as resistanc
title: Trump inspired a blue revolution. Can Democrats meet the moment? | Dana R Fisher

author: Suzanne Wrack
description:
Germany forward on her new life in London and drawing strength from the memory of her late brother, Dennis

Lisa Baum is 19, for the next few days at least, but you wouldn’t know it. The Germany forward plays with a maturity that explains why she was handed her Arsenal debut in their opening game of the season, less than two months after joining.

Baum had been told that the 2025 European champions had a vision for her but that coming in as a young player she would have to be patient. Ten minutes into her debut against Brighton, in Crawley, the young winger scored what would be the winning goal.

Continue reading...
title: Arsenal’s Lisa Baum: ‘I believe in us. I think it’s all about the small margins’

author: Jack Watson
description:
Cherry liqueur and chocolate syrup add an extra splash of indulgence to a time-honoured classic

This is inspired by both the classic old fashioned and the boozy-cherry-filled Mon Chéri chocolate. At Mr Fogg’s, we garnish it with a homemade version of the chocolate as well as the orange peel for an extra indulgent dash of sweetness and tartness, but that might be a step too far for a quiet Saturday night in at home.

Jack Watson, general manager, Mr Fogg’s Market Tavern, London WC2

Continue reading...
title: Cocktail of the week: Mr Fogg’s old fashioned adventurer – recipe | The good mixer

author: Katy Murrells
description:
ATP Finals updates from the afternoon action in Turin
Mail Katy | Kartal’s fightback against injury and abuse

And talking about Agassi: this is a lovely trip down memory lane of the 1990 season-ending final.

Buongiorno! With Carlos Alcaraz already guaranteed to finish top of the Ivan Lendl group after two straight-sets wins, the biggest jeopardy going into his match against the already-eliminated Flavio Cobolli is the state of his left hamstring. After picking up the injury against Daniil Medvedev on Wednesday, Alcaraz had an MRI scan yesterday and was cleared to play on, so now we’ll get to see if he can still hit the absurd levels he did earlier
title: Carlos Alcaraz v Flavio Cobolli: ATP Finals tennis group stage – live

author: Michael Aylwin
description:
Steve Tandy has made four changes to his team to face wounded Wallabies after heroics against All Blacks

They beat the All Blacks for the first time in 73 years and they make four changes. The Wales coaching team could barely have shrugged their shoulders with any more nonchalance after what the rest of us thought was a pretty spectacular achievement last weekend if they had picked their under-20s for Saturday night’s follow-up against Australia in Cardiff. But, no, they are actually adding depth as well as quality to this new generation tasked with keeping the creaking structures of Welsh rugby upright for the foreseeable.

If anything, the changes make the team stronger. No matter they are without Adam Beard (shoulder injury but hopefully back for the finals next weekend), they see fit to drop/rest/let-attend-birth-of-first-child three other players too, including the player of the match last weekend.
title: Rotated Wales aim to turn New Zealand miracle into true momentum against Australia

author: Bryony Moore, Elena Morresi, Stefania Orlando, Albert Villa Alsina and Sarah Bertram
description:
The war between the US, Israel and Iran has turned the strait of Hormuz, one of the world’s busiest oil shipping routes, into a battlefield, but also the centre of a deepening environmental disaster. Tankers struck by missiles or sea mines are leaking oil into the Gulf, leaving vast slicks visible from space, staining coastlines and threatening lasting damage to marine ecosystems. Many of these areas remain inaccessible because of the naval blockade, making it virtually impossible to document the devastation on the ground. The Guardian has examined dozens of satellite images and spoken to environmental experts in an effort to assess the scale of the damage

  • Oil slicks seen from space: the devastating impact of boat strikes on fragile Gulf ecosystems
title: How the war in Iran turned the Gulf into a climate catastrophe – video explainer

author: Presented by Jonathan Freedland , produced by Danielle Stephens and Nada Smiljanic
description:
Democrats who might be thinking of launching a presidential run in 2028 are starting to make moves. One such contender is Pete Buttigieg, the former transportation secretary under Joe Biden. Is he the candidate who can unite the broad church in his party?

There’s also talk that a vote to elect the new Senate leader could be moved up, helping Chuck Schumer retain power, after Chris Van Hollen challenged him for the position.

Jonathan Freedland speaks to Marianna Sotomayor of Puck News about the Democrats looking to shore up power on Capitol Hill and potentially head for the White House

Continue reading...
title: Could Pete Buttigieg win the White House in 2028? | Politics Weekly America

author: Laura Wilson
description:
The Taper Man by Nick Harkaway; Watch the Quiet Snow by Mick Herron; Revenge Plot by Stephanie Wrobel; The Voices of the Dead by Nicola Upson; The Bells of Fortune by Leonora Nattrass

The Taper Man by Nick Harkaway (Viking, £22)
The second George Smiley continuation novel from John le Carré’s son Nick Harkaway is set in 1965 and features early iterations of several characters who appear in Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy and Smiley’s People. The cold war is at its height, and British intelligence is keen to protect one of its most important sources, Red Army general Vladimir Vasilev. When a colleague is shot in Helsinki, Smiley discovers a connection to a group of Soviet agents who, through their links to a now defunct spying operation in the US, may jeopardise this key asset. Smiley
title: The best recent crime and thrillers – review roundup

author: Shaad D'Souza
description:
Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days?

From New York via Montana
Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G
Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November

Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Terrible things tend to happen, that’s the way the world works, and a person is defined by how they respond to each challenge. That goes for the knight in the forest and the characters in a film. author: Kathryn Hughes
description:
A gardener traces the dynasties that dominate the vegetal world in appropriately sumptuous prose

John Ruskin, the Victorian writer and critic, hated the way science insisted on turning his beloved natural world into something smutty. Botanists, he complained, used “microscopic malice” to reduce the spurs, petals and stamens of his favourite flowers to “obscene processes and prurient apparitions”. Others were less squeamish. In 1908, Marie Stopes, the scientist who later became a champion of birth control, spent three days in Japan’s Matsushima Bay in a state of “grand excitement” hunting ginkgo sperms. Oliver Sacks, the neurologist, passed his adolescence at Kew gawping at the cycads’ sexual organs. Reading Ben Dark’s excellent account, it is hard not to conclude that even the most modest plants are living in a state of permanent arousal.

Each of Dark’s chapters tells the story of one plant dynasty, from rootless, seedless pond scum to alpine meadows. Some 97%
